Machine Learning

1. What is Ignite ML?
  • Ignite ML is a distributed machine learning library built into Apache Ignite;
  • It trains models directly on data stored in Ignite — no ETL to external ML systems;
  • Algorithms run in a distributed fashion across cluster nodes using collocated computations;
  • Requires the ignite-ml module;
2. Key Benefits
  • Zero ETL — train on data where it lives; no need to export to Spark, Python, or another system;
  • Distributed training — algorithms are parallelized across cluster nodes;
  • Fault tolerance — if a node fails during training, the computation can recover;
  • Real-time inference — trained models can serve predictions with in-memory speed;
3. Supported Algorithms
CategoryAlgorithms
ClassificationLogistic Regression, SVM, k-NN, Decision Tree, Random Forest, Naive Bayes, ANN
RegressionLinear Regression, Decision Tree Regression, k-NN Regression
ClusteringK-Means, GMM
PreprocessingNormalization, Binarization, Imputation, encoding
Model SelectionCross-validation, Hyperparameter tuning
4. Basic ML Example
  • // Prepare training data in an Ignite cache
IgniteCache<Integer, double[]> trainingData = ...;

// Define a trainer
DecisionTreeClassificationTrainer trainer = new DecisionTreeClassificationTrainer();

// Train the model
DecisionTreeModel model = trainer.fit(
    ignite,
    trainingData,
    (k, v) -> VectorUtils.of(Arrays.copyOfRange(v, 0, v.length - 1)), // features
    (k, v) -> v[v.length - 1]                                          // label
);

// Make predictions
double prediction = model.predict(VectorUtils.of(5.1, 3.5, 1.4, 0.2));
5. Pipeline API
  • Chain preprocessing and training into a pipeline: 
    Pipeline pipeline = new Pipeline()
    .addPreprocessingTrainer(new MinMaxScalerTrainer())
    .addTrainer(new LogisticRegressionSGDTrainer());

PipelineMdl model = pipeline.fit(ignite, trainingData, featureExtractor, labelExtractor);

double prediction = model.predict(inputVector);
6. When to Use Ignite ML
  • When your data is already in Ignite and you want to avoid moving it to an external ML platform;
  • When you need low-latency inference directly from the cache;
  • For simpler ML tasks (classification, regression, clustering) that fit the built-in algorithms;
  • For complex deep learning, consider exporting data to TensorFlow/PyTorch (Ignite has a TensorFlow integration);
